svg.aria-label: A flow diagram of the four steps performed by _aead_recvmsg() on the AEAD decryption path, with byte offsets marked on every buffer. Three lengths are computed first: used is every transmit byte the caller has sent, outlen is used minus the authentication size, and processed is the number of transmit bytes the request consumes, so that processed minus the authentication size equals outlen. Step one builds the receive scatterlist from the caller's iovecs, pinning the caller's own pages and reserving one spare table entry. Step two copies the first outlen bytes, the associated data and the ciphertext, from the transmit list into those pages through the null cipher. Step three releases the copied transmit entries and reassigns the remaining tag entries, covering the byte range from processed minus the authentication size to processed, into a per-request array, moving the page pointers rather than copying the pages. Step four clears the terminator on the receive list and chains it to that array, so the tag entries sit at destination offset outlen. The request is then submitted with the same list as both source and destination.
svg.title: The four steps of _aead_recvmsg() on the decrypt path
svg.desc: A vertical flow of four numbered steps, each paired with a buffer diagram carrying byte offsets. The lengths used, outlen and processed are defined first, with the identity processed minus authsize equals outlen. Step one pins the caller's receive pages and reserves a spare scatterlist entry for a later link. Step two copies associated data and ciphertext into those pages through the null cipher. Step three moves the tag entries out of the shared transmit list into a per-request array without copying the pages. Step four chains that array onto the end of the receive list, placing page-cache memory at destination offset outlen. A closing panel shows the submitted request, whose source and destination arguments name the same list.

g.text: THE FOUR STEPS OF _aead_recvmsg() ON THE DECRYPT PATH
FIRST, THREE LENGTHS — NO MEMORY IS TOUCHED YET
every TX byte the caller has sent: AAD ‖ CT ‖ Tag
the output region the caller receives: AAD ‖ PT
the TX bytes this request consumes — so processed - as == outlen
— turn the caller's recvmsg(2) iovecs into the RX SGL
af_alg_make_sg() pins the caller's own userspace pages; the sg table gets one entry more than the page count.
“Add one extra for linking” — reserved for step 4
Copies the first outlen bytes — AAD ‖ CT — into the RX pages, driven through the ecb(cipher_null) transformation.
Releases the TX entries already copied and reassigns the rest — the tag, at [processed - as, processed) — into a
per-request array. The pages are not copied: the same struct page pointers move, with offset and length adjusted.
the page-cache pages that splice(2) put on the source side,
now held in a per-request array of their own
Clears the terminator on the last RX entry and writes the link into the spare slot reserved in step 1, so a walk of
the RX list runs off its own end and continues into areq->tsgl.
Both the source and the destination argument name this one list — everything from offset outlen onward is page-cache memory.
